brief:
Israel has suspended operations of 37 international humanitarian organizations in Gaza, according to Dawn, dismantling critical aid infrastructure as the humanitarian crisis deepens. The move, initiated nearly a year ago, has shifted the aid debate beyond logistics like truck crossings to fundamental questions about how Palestinians access assistance.

The suspensions have gutted the operational capacity of organizations that coordinate food distribution, medical care, and emergency services across the Strip. Aid groups warn the closures have created gaps in humanitarian coverage that Palestinian health and welfare systems cannot fill on their own.
dek: Nearly a year after Israel moved to suspend the operations of 37 international humanitarian organizations in Gaza, the question of aid has evolved beyond how many trucks enter the Strip or the total aid that reaches Palestinians.
title: Israel suspends operations of 37 international aid groups in Gaza
